text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The monetary development in the first quarter of this year is in line with the National Bank of Slovakia's (NBS) monetary programme, NBS Governor Vladimir Masar said.
- Masar said the overall amount of credits rose by 12 percent, year-on-year, in the first three months of the year.

- The Economics Ministry estimates the required investments to develop Slovakia's engineering sector at some 5.15 billion crowns by the year 2000, and at about 2.94 billion crowns between the years 2001 and 2005.

- Private bank PKB posted a 1996 profit of 160.1 million crowns, but it did not say whether this was a pre-tax or after-tax result. PKB plans to increase its balance sum by three billion crowns to 16 billion in 1997.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The government is expected to discuss a basic strategy designed to solve problems with the trade balance at its regular Tuesday session.
- Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said imposing quotas on unspecified imports could be one of the measures to help improve the trade balance but he ruled out re-imposing an import surcharge.

- Kozlik said the so called "zero variant", according to which the Czech Republic and Slovakia would withdraw their claims against each other from the split of the common state in 1993, would be acceptable both for Prague and Bratislava, but that the Czech side shows little political will to come to such a conclusion.

- The government, employees association and trade unions have agreed to a seven percent increase of wages at state budget funded organisations, effective July 1. Wages of doctors should be increased by an average 35 percent from April.
SME - The state regulation of motor fuel prices should be cancelled in the near future, the finance ministry said.
